name: Basque-Amerindian Pidgin
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct trade pidgin known from fragmentary lexical records; no phonological description exists to consult for stress.

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter, Gidor Bilbao, Nicolaas G. H. Deen & Jose Ignacio Hualde. 1991. Basque pidgins in Iceland and Canada. Anejos del ASJU XXIII. Donostia: Gipuzkoako Foru Aldundia. 172 pp. Contains Bakker, 'La lengua de las tribus costeras es medio vasca': Un pidgin vasco y amerindio utilizado por europeos y nativos americanos en Norteamerica, h. 1540-h. 1640, pp. 137-165 (Spanish version of Bakker 1989 Anthropological Linguistics).
sources.note: Section 6.3 'Rasgos foneticos y morfologicos del pidgin' (pp. 154-155) states that only isolated words and short phrases survive, so the author limits himself to phonetics and morphology: liquids > r, some labial stops > m, palatalization of s, i/o > u, plus the morphemes -a and -koa. No mention of stress/accent in the Canadian chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned text for stress/accent/acento/prosod finds nothing); Hualde's chapter on the Icelandic Basque pidgin (pp. 123-133) is likewise silent.

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter. 1988. Basque pidgin vocabulary in European-Algonquian trade contacts. Papers of the Nineteenth Algonquian Conference (Algonquian Papers - Archive 19), ed. W. Cowan, pp. 7-15. Ottawa: Carleton University.
sources.note: Section 5.2 'Phonological Processes' (p. 11) lists only segmental adaptations (Basque l, r > r; initial p, b > m; alveolar/palatal sibilants not distinguished; intervocalic voicing). Nothing on stress, accent or prosody anywhere in the 9-page article; data are isolated words and short phrases from 17th-c. French/Jesuit sources.
sources.venue: Papers of the Nineteenth Algonquian Conference (Algonquian Papers - Archive 19), ed

sources.note: No references listed at all for this languoid; status extinct; links to Wikipedia 'Algonquian-Basque pidgin', whose reference list is the four Bakker items above plus Mithun 1999 and which itself notes no stress information.

sources.citation: Bakker, Peter. 1996. Language contact and pidginization in Davis Strait, Hudson Strait, and the Gulf of Saint Lawrence (northeast Canada). In E. H. Jahr & I. Broch (eds), Language contact in the Arctic: Northern pidgins and contact languages, 261-310. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
